name: Ashford

neighbourhoods.name: Ashford town centre
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces and flats around the centre, with modern apartment blocks near the international station.

neighbourhoods.name: Kennington
neighbourhoods.housing: Interwar and post-war semis and detached houses on the north side of the town.

neighbourhoods.name: Willesborough
neighbourhoods.housing: A mix of older cottages, post-war estates and newer housing to the east of the town.

neighbourhoods.name: Singleton and Park Farm
neighbourhoods.housing: Estates of modern houses built from the 1980s onwards on the edge of Ashford.

neighbourhoods.name: Tenterden
neighbourhoods.housing: Weatherboarded and brick period houses along the high street, with newer homes around it.

neighbourhoods.name: Wye
neighbourhoods.housing: Period cottages and village houses below the North Downs.

neighbourhoods.name: Charing
neighbourhoods.housing: Historic village houses and cottages on the edge of the downs.

neighbourhoods.name: Hamstreet
neighbourhoods.housing: Village houses and bungalows near the Romney Marsh edge.

neighbourhoods.name: Woodchurch
neighbourhoods.housing: Cottages and detached houses in a rural Weald village.

neighbourhoods.name: Appledore
neighbourhoods.housing: Period cottages and village houses near the Royal Military Canal.

housing: Ashford borough is a growing market town surrounded by Weald and Romney Marsh countryside. The town has expanded fast, with large new-build estates and apartment blocks near the international station, alongside Victorian terraces in the centre. Outside the town are timber-framed, weatherboarded and brick cottages in villages such as Tenterden, Wye and Charing. Private rented homes range from town-centre flats let to commuters to rural cottages.
checkinTips: Weatherboarded and timber-framed cottages in Tenterden and the Weald villages: photograph external boarding, window frames and any rot or flaking paint.
Rural homes off mains gas: photograph oil tanks, the gauge reading and any septic tank or treatment plant access cover.
Apartment blocks near the international station: note fob, key and parking permit counts, and photograph the meter cupboard and bin store.
New-build estates such as Singleton and Park Farm: photograph sealant around baths and showers, settlement cracks and the condition of gardens and fences.
Old cottages with low beams and uneven floors: photograph beams, floorboards and door frames so later damage can be compared.
tenantHelp: Tenants in Ashford can contact Ashford Borough Council’s private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in a rented home.
